title: The constructed heart inverse-image comparison respects composition
statement: The constructed heart inverse-image comparison respects composition. For f:X→Y and g:Y→Z, normalized encodings EX,EY,EZ, and every internal R_Z-module M, heart_X(c_internal(f,g)_M);heartPull_f(upperStar_R(g)(M));upperStar_A(f)(heartPull_g(M)) equals heartPull_(f;g)(M);c_ordinary(f,g)_(heart_Z(M)). Both compositors are the published underived ones; there is no derived category, boundedness, properness, or qcqs assumption.

source.place: Transport and clause (2); inverse-image coefficient encoding, steps 1--3.

proof.text: Forget scalar actions and evaluate the two composites of heartPush on sections. Its constituent comparison maps are identities; both composite direct-image maps are induced by the same canonical base-change isomorphism. Faithfulness yields the direct-image composition equation.

Apply injectivity of mateEquiv to the two pasted inverse-image squares. Its compatibility with horizontal pasting and with conjugation turns them into the direct-image equation. The published inverse-image compositors conjugate to the direct-image compositors. Evaluate the resulting square and cancel the inverses of heartPull to obtain the displayed equation.

theorem heartPull_comp (e : Mon.mk R ≅ Mon.mk (coefficient A))
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (EX : Encoding A X) (EY : Encoding A Y) (EZ : Encoding A Z)
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj R Z)) :
    (heart A R e X EX).map ((CondensedRing.upperStarComp R f g).hom.app M) ≫
      (heartPull A R e f EX EY).hom.app ((CondensedRing.upperStar R g).obj M) ≫
      (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) f).map
        ((heartPull A R e g EY EZ).hom.app M) =
    (heartPull A R e (f ≫ g) EX EZ).hom.app M ≫
      (upperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) f g).hom.app
        ((heart A R e Z EZ).obj M)
